title: Tokyo
subtitle: 7 Days of Neon Nights, Street Food & Cultural Wonders for the Whole Group
description: Seven action-packed days in the world's most electric city — from the anime paradise of Akihabara and the vintage fashion chaos of Harajuku to peaceful Meiji Shrine, bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, teamLab digital art, and some of the best ramen, sushi, and izakaya nights on the planet. August in Tokyo means summer festivals, yukata-clad crowds, and golden evening light over the skyline.
bestFor: Group of 5+ exploring Tokyo for the first time (or returning for more)
highlights: Shibuya Crossing scramble — the world's busiest intersection
Senso-ji Temple at dusk — lanterns glowing over Asakusa
teamLab Planets Toyosu — digital art immersion
Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh seafood at dawn
Shinjuku izakaya crawl — yakitori, beer, and midnight ramen
Akihabara electric town — anime, gaming, and tech overload
Harajuku & Omotesando — fashion, crepes, and luxury boutiques

essentials.title: ☀️ August in Tokyo — Summer Festival Season
essentials.text: August is peak summer in Tokyo — hot (30-35°C / 86-95°F), humid, but incredibly vibrant. This is festival season: Bon Odori dances, Sumida River fireworks, and neighborhood matsuri (summer festivals) everywhere. Pack lightweight, breathable clothing. Convenience stores (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Lawson) are lifesavers for cold drinks, ice cream, and AC breaks. Typhoon season starts in August — keep an eye on weather apps.

essentials.title: 🚇 Getting Around — IC Card & Subway
essentials.text: Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at any JR station (¥500 deposit). Works on all trains, subways, buses, and convenience stores. The Tokyo Metro Day Pass (¥600 adults) is great if you're doing 3+ metro rides a day. For airport: Narita Express (N'EX) from Narita is about ¥3,000 each way; Haneda takes the Keikyu Line for ¥600. Google Maps is excellent for Tokyo transit navigation.

essentials.title: 💰 Budget Tips for Groups
essentials.text: Tokyo is actually manageable for groups. Set lunch menus (teishoku) at sit-down restaurants run ¥800-1,500. Convenience store meals are ¥300-700 and legitimately good. Ramen shops typically ¥900-1,300. Many great izakayas have flat-rate all-you-can-drink plans for ¥1,500-2,000/person for 2 hours. Booking restaurants online (TableAll, Tablecheck, or directly) is recommended for groups of 5+.

essentials.title: 📱 Connectivity & Useful Apps
essentials.text: Get a pocket WiFi rental (Ninja WiFi or Global Advanced Communications) or SIM card at the airport. Apps: Google Maps (transit), Google Translate (camera mode for menus!), Hyperdia (train timing), Tabelog (restaurant reviews in Japanese — Google Translate helps), and LINE (local messaging). Most train announcements are in English and Japanese.

days.title: Arrival & Shinjuku Exploration
days.description: Touch down, get your IC cards sorted, and dive straight into Shinjuku — Tokyo's most frenetic neighborhood. Walk the neon-lit streets, browse the department stores, and end the night with an izakaya crawl through Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho).

activities.title: ✈️ Arrive & Get Your IC Card
activities.description: Clear customs and head to the JR ticket office or IC card machine. Load ¥3,000-5,000 on your Suica or Pasmo. Take the Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus to your hotel in Shinjuku area.
details: 🚃 Narita Express to Shinjuku: ~90 min, ¥3,070/person
🚌 Limousine Bus: ~90-120 min, ¥3,200/person (easier for groups with luggage)
💳 Suica/Pasmo card: ¥500 deposit + load your desired amount
🏨 Check in, freshen up, store luggage if needed

tips.text: 💡 The Limousine Bus is worth it for groups of 5+ with suitcases — much easier than navigating trains with luggage.

activities.title: 🌃 Shinjuku Night Walk
activities.description: Stroll from East Shinjuku (Kabukicho entertainment district, Don Quijote, Godzilla statue) to the quieter Golden Gai area of tiny vintage bars, each seating 5-8 people.
details: 📍 Kabukicho entrance arch: East exit of Shinjuku Station
🦕 Godzilla head peeking from Hotel Gracery rooftop — iconic photo spot
🍻 Golden Gai: narrow alleys of ~200 tiny bars — each has a unique theme

activities.title: 🍢 Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane)
activities.description: Ducking into Tokyo's famous 'Memory Lane' — a smoky alley of yakitori grills dating back to post-war Tokyo. Order skewers of chicken, offal, and veggies washed down with cold beer or shochu highballs.
details: 📍 Just outside the west exit of Shinjuku Station
💰 Budget ¥2,000-3,000/person for yakitori + drinks
⏰ Most stalls open from 5pm, best 7-10pm
🌟 Classic spots: Asadachi, Kebab-Ya

meals.name: Omoide Yokocho Yakitori
meals.description: Smoky skewers and cold beer in Tokyo's most atmospheric alley

tips.text: 💡 Groups of 5+ may need to split across 2-3 tiny stalls in Memory Lane — embrace it and meet back at the alley entrance.

days.title: Harajuku, Meiji Shrine & Shibuya
days.description: Morning serenity at Meiji Shrine through the towering torii gates, then into the wild fashion chaos of Takeshita Street in Harajuku, upscale Omotesando boutiques, and the evening spectacle of Shibuya Crossing.

activities.title: ⛩️ Meiji Jingu Shrine
activities.description: A forested oasis in central Tokyo. Walk the gravel path lined by towering camphor trees to Japan's most important Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Arrive early to catch the peaceful morning atmosphere.
details: 📍 1-1 Yoyogikamizono-cho, Shibuya — 5 min walk from Harajuku Station
⏰ Opens at sunrise (5:00am in August), closes ~18:30
💴 Free entry to grounds. Inner sanctuary: ¥500/person
🕐 Allow 45 min to 1 hour for the full walk

activities.title: 🎀 Takeshita Street, Harajuku
activities.description: The birthplace of Japanese street fashion. A narrow pedestrian street packed with vintage clothing, kawaii accessories, crepe stands, and every conceivable fashion subculture. Pure sensory overload — in the best way.
details: 📍 Takeshita-dori, 1 min from Harajuku Station (Chiyoda line side)
🥞 Marion Crepes (since 1977) — strawberry cream crepe is a must
👗 Best vintage: 2nd Street, Kinji, Chicago vintage
💡 Go mid-morning on weekdays to avoid the worst crowds

meals.name: Convenience Store Breakfast
meals.description: Hit a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near your hotel for onigiri, egg sandwiches, and canned coffee

activities.title: 🛍️ Omotesando Hills & Architecture Walk
activities.description: Stroll 'Tokyo's Champs-Élysées' — tree-lined Omotesando boulevard with flagship stores from Prada, Louis Vuitton, Dior, and the stunning Omotesando Hills mall designed by Tadao Ando. Window shopping at minimum.
details: 🏗️ Prada Aoyama: Herzog & de Meuron glass facade — free to look
🏛️ Omotesando Hills: undulating spiral atrium
☕ Omotesando Koffee — tiny coffee kiosk inside a townhouse, famous for cube-shaped koffee jelly

activities.title: 🚦 Shibuya Crossing at Dusk
activities.description: Time your arrival at Shibuya for the magic hour — as dusk falls, the crossing becomes an electric symphony of humanity. Scramble with the crowd (up to 3,000 people cross at once), then watch from above at Shibuya Sky or the Starbucks second floor overlooking the crossing.
details: 📍 In front of Hachiko statue, Shibuya Station
🏙️ Best views from above: Shibuya Sky (¥2,000), or Mag's Park free deck
🐕 Hachiko statue — iconic meeting point and photo op
⏰ Most dramatic 6-9pm when evening rush meets the lit signs

meals.name: Afuri Ramen, Harajuku
meals.description: Yuzu shio ramen — light, citrusy broth that's perfect for hot August days

meals.name: Ichiran or Fuunji Ramen, Shinjuku/Shibuya
meals.description: Solo booth ramen at Ichiran, or standout tsukemen (dipping noodles) at Fuunji

tips.text: 💡 Shibuya Sky rooftop closes in bad weather — check conditions on the day. Alternatively, the 2nd floor window at the Starbucks overlooking the crossing is free.

days.title: Asakusa, Tsukiji & Akihabara
days.description: Wake up early for fresh seafood at Tsukiji Outer Market, spend the morning in old-school Asakusa with Senso-ji Temple and the Nakamise shopping street, then geek out in Akihabara's electric town.

activities.title: 🍣 Tsukiji Outer Market Breakfast
activities.description: The inner tuna auction moved to Toyosu, but Tsukiji's outer market remains Tokyo's best food street. Arrive 7-9am for fresh sashimi sets, tamagoyaki (sweet egg roll), fresh oysters, and ocean-fresh uni on rice. The vendors here have been doing this for decades.
details: 📍 Tsukiji, Chuo — 5 min walk from Tsukiji-shijo Station (Oedo line)
⏰ Most stalls open 5am-2pm; best selection before 10am
🥚 Tamagoyaki at Yamachō or Marutoyo — freshly grilled ¥300-500
🦪 Fresh oysters: 3 for ¥500-700 at Tsuruhachi
🍱 Sashimi donburi: ¥1,500-2,500 — various stalls

meals.name: Tsukiji Market Seafood Breakfast
meals.description: Fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, oysters, and seafood don at the outer market

tips.text: 💡 Stalls are packed on weekends. Arrive by 7:30am for the best selection and shortest waits.

activities.title: 🏮 Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise-dori
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple. Pass through the Kaminarimon gate (the famous giant lantern), browse the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks, ceramics, and souvenirs, and explore the main hall where incense smoke swirls year-round.
details: 📍 2-3-1 Asakusa, Taito — 5 min walk from Asakusa Station
⏰ Temple grounds always open, main hall 6am-5pm
💴 Free entry to the grounds
🍡 Try ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes) and ningyo-yaki from the Nakamise stalls
👘 Rent yukata near the temple for the full summer festival look (¥2,000-4,000)

activities.title: 🌊 Sumida River Walk & Asakusa Street Food
activities.description: Wander down to the Sumida River where the Azumabashi bridge offers great views of the Asahi Beer Hall (the famous golden 'flame' building) and a glimpse of Tokyo Skytree rising in the distance.
details: 📍 Azumabashi bridge, 5 min from Senso-ji
🍺 Asahi 'Golden Flame' building — iconic Tokyo oddity
🗼 Tokyo Skytree visible in the background

activities.title: 🎮 Akihabara — Anime, Gaming & Gadgets
activities.description: The spiritual home of anime, manga, retro games, and electronics. Multi-floor arcades, maid cafes, doujinshi shops, gashapon machines, and flagship stores like Yodobashi Camera (8 floors of electronics) and Animate (anime merch). Sensory overload guaranteed.
details: 📍 Akihabara Station, Chiyoda/JR Yamanote lines
🕹️ Super Potato — legendary retro game store (floors 3-6 are wild)
🤖 Gundam Café — giant Gundam robot + themed food
☕ Maidreamin Maid Café — the classic maid café experience (¥500-1,500)
🎯 Taito HEY arcade — stacked with classic arcade machines and UFO catchers

meals.name: Kanda Yabu Soba
meals.description: Historic soba shop near Akihabara, operating since 1880 — cold zarusoba or hot kakesoba

tips.text: 💡 Exchange leftover foreign cash at the Akihabara post office — good rates and no commission.

days.title: teamLab & Odaiba Digital Day
days.description: An immersive day at teamLab Planets Toyosu — one of the world's most impressive digital art installations — then across the rainbow bridge to Odaiba's futuristic artificial island for sunset views, the Gundam statue, and dinner.

activities.title: 🌊 teamLab Planets Toyosu
activities.description: Walk through knee-deep water that becomes an infinite mirror of koi fish, float through forests of hanging flowers, and lose yourself in crystal-clear light rooms. One of the most photographed art experiences in the world. Book well in advance — sells out weeks ahead for August.
details: 📍 6-1-16 Toyosu, Koto — 5 min walk from Shin-Toyosu Station
⏰ Opens 9am daily
💴 ¥3,200 adults, ¥1,000 children (7-15) — MUST book online in advance
👗 Wear shorts or roll up pants — you walk through water (ankle-to-knee depth)
📱 Book at: planets.teamlab.art/en/
⏱️ Allow 90 min to 2 hours

meals.name: Convenience Store at Shin-Toyosu Station
meals.description: Grab onigiri and coffee from the Lawson inside the station before entering teamLab

tips.text: 💡 For a group of 5+, book teamLab Planets tickets 2-3 weeks before your trip — August is peak season and they sell out. Check planets.teamlab.art/en/

activities.title: 🤖 Gundam Statue at DiverCity
activities.description: A life-size (18m tall) RX-93ff Hi-Nu Gundam robot stands guard outside DiverCity Tokyo Plaza. Free to see. Especially spectacular at night when it lights up.
details: 📍 DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, 1-1-10 Aomi, Koto
⏰ Freely viewable anytime; light shows on weekends 17:00, 19:00, 20:00
🛍️ DiverCity is a mall with good food court if you want lunch

activities.title: 🌅 Odaiba Waterfront & Rainbow Bridge
activities.description: Stroll the Odaiba waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Statue of Liberty replica. As the sun sets over Tokyo Bay, the bridges and skyline turn golden. Great group photo location.
details: 📍 Odaiba Seaside Park — free
🗽 Statue of Liberty replica at Daiba Park — quirky Tokyo touch
🌉 Rainbow Bridge illuminates after dark — beautiful from the waterfront

meals.name: DiverCity Food Court
meals.description: Large food court with ramen, sushi, tempura, and more — great for groups with different preferences

meals.name: Zenya Izakaya, Odaiba
meals.description: Classic izakaya with bay views — great for large groups, all-you-can-drink plans available

days.title: Ueno, Yanaka & Ikebukuro
days.description: Explore Tokyo's cultural heart at Ueno Park and its world-class museums, then get lost in Yanaka — one of the last old Shitamachi (low city) neighborhoods to survive Tokyo's transformation. End in Ikebukuro for Pokémon Center and night entertainment.

activities.title: 🏛️ Tokyo National Museum (Ueno)
activities.description: Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing the world's largest collection of Japanese art and antiquities — samurai armor, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculpture, and paintings going back thousands of years. Even a quick 90-minute visit is jaw-dropping.
details: 📍 13-9 Ueno Park, Taito — 10 min walk from Ueno Station
⏰ 9:30am-5pm (Fri/Sat until 8pm), closed Mondays
💴 ¥1,000 adults, free under 18
🌟 Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is the must-see main building

activities.title: 🦒 Ueno Zoo (Optional for Families)
activities.description: If anyone in your group loves animals, Japan's oldest zoo is right in Ueno Park — home to giant pandas, gorillas, and hundreds of species.
details: 📍 9-83 Ueno Park, Taito
💴 ¥600 adults, ¥200 children
🐼 Giant pandas: Xiao Xiao and Lei Lei (born 2021) are the stars

meals.name: Ueno Ameyoko Market
meals.description: Morning stroll through the legendary Ameyoko street market for taiyaki, fresh fruit, and snacks before the museums

activities.title: 🏘️ Yanaka Ginza & Yanaka Cemetery
activities.description: Yanaka survived the Great Kanto Earthquake and WWII bombing raids, leaving Tokyo's most preserved old-town neighborhood. Wander the Yanaka Ginza shopping street (try menchi-katsu — deep-fried ground pork cutlet from local butchers), peek into old temples, and stroll through the historic cemetery.
details: 📍 Yanaka-ginza: 3-13 Yanaka, Taito — 10 min walk from Nippori Station
🍖 Menchi-katsu at Niku no Suzuki — legendary local snack, ¥200-300
⛩️ Tennō-ji Temple in the cemetery — classic old Tokyo vibe
🐱 Yanaka is famous for its stray cats — you'll spot them everywhere

meals.name: Kayaba Coffee, Yanaka
meals.description: A beautifully preserved 1930s coffee shop that survived the war. Tamago sando (egg sandwich) and coffee

tips.text: 💡 Yanaka is easy to combine with Nezu Shrine (famous for its small, winding torii tunnel) — just a 10-minute walk away.

activities.title: 🎮 Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo & Sunshine City
activities.description: The flagship Pokémon Center on the second floor of Sunshine City mall in Ikebukuro — the largest in Japan. Plushies, trading cards, clothing, keychains, and all the Pokémon merchandise you could want.
details: 📍 Sunshine City Alpa, 3-1-1 Higashiikebukuro, Toshima — 3F
⏰ 10am-8pm daily
💡 Also check Animate Ikebukuro (7 floors of anime merch) one block away
🎡 J-WORLD indoor theme park is in the same building

meals.name: Ikebukuro Gyoza Stadium or Nishiikebukuro Park Izakaya
meals.description: Ikebukuro's famous gyoza hall with multiple competing gyoza styles, or the izakaya restaurants surrounding Nishiikebukuro Park

days.title: Shibuya Sky, Shimokitazawa & Night Ramen
days.description: A Tokyo deep-cut day: the vintage bohemian streets of Shimokitazawa, the boutique cafes and bookstores of Daikanyama, and the canal-side restaurants of Nakameguro. End with rooftop views and late-night ramen.

activities.title: 🎸 Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's Coolest Neighborhood
activities.description: A labyrinth of narrow lanes filled with vintage clothing stores, live music venues, coffee shops, and indie boutiques. Beloved by musicians, artists, and students. This is Tokyo with its guard down — relaxed, creative, and refreshingly un-touristy.
details: 📍 Shimokitazawa Station, Odakyu/Keio Inokashira lines
👗 Best vintage: RAG TAG, New York Joe Exchange, Flamingo
☕ Bear Pond Espresso — cult-status specialty coffee
🎵 Walk around randomly — new murals and tiny shops around every corner

meals.name: Bear Pond Espresso or Café Kitasando
meals.description: Shimokitazawa's specialty coffee scene — tiny roaster cafes with excellent single-origin brews

activities.title: 📚 Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books)
activities.description: One of the most beautiful bookstores in the world — a complex of three buildings with curated books, vinyl records, magazines, a café, and a specialty coffee bar. Great for a peaceful hour of browsing.
details: 📍 17-5 Sarugakucho, Shibuya
⏰ 7am-2am daily
☕ Anjin coffee bar inside — excellent pour-overs
📖 Books are mostly Japanese but the design and atmosphere transcend language

activities.title: 🌿 Nakameguro Canal Walk
activities.description: The Meguro River canal lined with cherry trees (bare in August, but the boutique restaurants and cafes along the banks are fabulous year-round). Some of Tokyo's best independent coffee shops, restaurants, and concept stores line this stretch.
details: 📍 Nakameguro Station, Tokyu Toyoko line
☕ Onibus Coffee — roaster café on the canal
🍜 Fuunji, Nakameguro — the best tsukemen (dipping ramen) in Tokyo
🌊 Stroll from Nakameguro Station east toward Daikanyama — ~20 min walk

meals.name: Izakaya Lunch Set Near Daikanyama
meals.description: Many izakayas open for lunch with set menus at half the dinner price — grilled fish, rice, miso, pickles

activities.title: 🌃 Shibuya Sky Observation Deck
activities.description: Shibuya Scramble Square's rooftop observatory — 230 meters up, with 360-degree views of Tokyo including Shinjuku, Mt. Fuji on clear days, and the dazzling Shibuya Crossing below. Book sunset time slot.
details: 📍 2-24-12 Shibuya — top of Shibuya Scramble Square
⏰ 10am-11pm (last entry 10:30pm)
💴 ¥2,000 adults — book online (hoshizora.museum/shibuyasky/en/)
📸 Clear days: Mt. Fuji visible to the west at golden hour

activities.title: 🍜 Midnight Ramen at Ichiran or Fuunji
activities.description: Tokyo doesn't sleep. End the night with a bowl of ramen at 1am — it's perfectly normal. Ichiran's solo-booth concept is the full experience.
details: 📍 Ichiran Shibuya: 1-22-7 Jinnan, Shibuya — open 24 hours
🍜 Tonkotsu broth, firm noodles, customize everything via order form

meals.name: Izakaya Dinner, Shibuya/Nakameguro
meals.description: Group izakaya dinner — order-by-tablet, all-you-can-drink plans for 2 hours, massive food selection

tips.text: 💡 Shibuya Sky is popular — book your sunset time slot online at least 2-3 days ahead, especially in August.

days.title: Nikko Day Trip & Farewell Dinner
days.description: A day trip to Nikko — the ornate UNESCO shrine complex 2 hours from Tokyo, set in cedar-forested mountains — followed by a proper farewell dinner back in Tokyo.

activities.title: ⛩️ Nikko Toshō-gū Shrine Complex
activities.description: Nikko is the complete opposite of Tokyo — ancient, forested, and breathtakingly ornate. The Toshō-gū shrine, built to honor Tokugawa Ieyasu, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site dripping in gold leaf, intricate carvings, and crimson lacquer. The famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys are here.
details: 🚃 Take the Tōbu Nikkō Line from Asakusa Station — ~2 hours, ¥1,400 with Tōbu pass
⏰ Toshō-gū: 8am-5pm in summer
💴 Toshō-gū complex pass: ¥1,300 adults
🌿 Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine also on the same pass
🦷 Don't miss: the famous Sleeping Cat (Nemuri-neko) carving and the Yomeimon Gate

activities.title: 🌊 Kegon Falls (Optional)
activities.description: A 30-minute bus ride from Nikko shrines to Lake Chuzenji and the 97-meter Kegon Waterfall — one of Japan's three greatest waterfalls. Beautiful in August with full greenery.
details: 🚌 Bus from Nikko Sogo Bus Terminal: 45 min, ¥1,150
🌊 Kegon Falls elevator to base: ¥570
💡 The waterfall viewing is free from the top; elevator gives the dramatic bottom-up view

meals.name: Hippari Dako, Nikko
meals.description: Famous udon shop in Nikko with yuba (tofu skin) — a local specialty. Cheap, filling, and delicious

tips.text: 💡 Buy the Tobu Nikko Pass (¥4,300) which includes round-trip train from Asakusa + unlimited buses in Nikko for 2 days. For a group of 5+, this saves significantly.

activities.title: 🥩 Farewell Yakiniku or Sushi Dinner, Shinjuku
activities.description: Send off Tokyo properly — either premium yakiniku (grilled wagyu at your own table grill) at a dedicated restaurant, or an omakase sushi experience. Both are best booked in advance for groups.
details: 🥩 Yakiniku: Kintan or Gyu-Kaku near Shinjuku — ¥3,000-5,000/person
🍣 Sushi: Mori no Sushi or Zauo (fishing sushi restaurant — catch your fish) — ¥3,000-6,000/person
📅 Book in advance via TableAll.com for English-language reservations

activities.title: 🛍️ Last-Minute Shopping & Konbini Haul
activities.description: Stock up on omiyage (souvenirs/gifts) at Don Quijote, Isetan department store, or any convenience store. Kit Kat flavors, Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito cookies, and Pocky varieties are popular choices.
details: 🛒 Don Quijote Shinjuku: open 24 hours — tax-free shopping for non-residents
🍫 Isetan B2 food floor — premium wagashi, high-end confectionery
🏪 Any konbini for budget snacks and quirky Japanese candy to bring home

meals.name: Farewell Yakiniku at Kintan or Gyu-Kaku
meals.description: Go out in style — wagyu beef at your own grill, unlimited side dishes, cold beer or sake

tips.text: 💡 Most shops offer tax-free (8-10%) purchases for tourists on purchases over ¥5,000 — bring your passport.
